headword: お{招|まね}きにあずかる
gloss: to be kindly invited; to receive an invitation (humble/formal)

definitions.gloss: to be kindly invited; to receive an invitation — a formal, humble way of acknowledging that one has been invited by the addressee or by a person the speaker respects
definitions.explanation: A set phrase combining お{招|まね}き ('invitation', with the honorific prefix お) and あずかる ('to be granted, to partake of [something offered]', used humbly to receive a favor). Speakers use it to gratefully acknowledge having been invited somewhere, treating the invitation itself as a favor extended to them. Common in formal speeches, thank-you remarks at weddings, parties, and official gatherings.

examples.japanese: お{招|まね}きにあずかりまして、⟦ありがとうございます→ありがとうございます：09886_arigatougozaimasu⟧。
examples.english: Thank you very much for kindly inviting me.

examples.japanese: ⟦{本日|ほんじつ}→本日：09643_honjitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お{招|まね}きにあずかり、⟦{光栄|こうえい}→光栄：19436_kouei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{存|ぞん}じます→存じる：05912_zonjiru⟧。
examples.english: It is an honor to have been invited today.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧たび⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{結婚披露宴|けっこんひろうえん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{招|まね}きにあずかり、⟦{誠|まこと}→誠：27623_makoto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ありがとうございます→ありがとうございます：09886_arigatougozaimasu⟧。
examples.english: Thank you so very much for inviting me to this wedding reception.

notes:
A formal, humble set phrase used by a guest to acknowledge the host's invitation with gratitude. The あずかる here carries its humble meaning of 'to be granted' or 'to receive (something favorable)'.

USAGE:
- Most at home as the opening line of a formal thank-you speech, a toast, or a polite email reply.
- Often continues with ⟦ありがとうございます→ありがとうございます：09886_arigatougozaimasu⟧, ⟦{光栄|こうえい}→光栄：19436_kouei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{存|ぞん}じます→存じる：05912_zonjiru⟧, or a similar polite expression of gratitude.
- Not used in casual speech; among friends, plain ⟦{呼|よ}んで→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧⟦くれて→くれる：00724_kureru⟧⟦ありがとう→ありがとう：00917_arigatou⟧ or ⟦{招|まね}いて→招く：02425_maneku⟧⟦くれて→くれる：00724_kureru⟧⟦ありがとう→ありがとう：00917_arigatou⟧ is used instead.
- The speaker places themselves below the host, so this phrase is appropriate when the host is a superior, client, or honored acquaintance, or when the setting itself (wedding, ceremony) calls for formal speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{招|まね}きにあずかり、⟦ありがとうございます→ありがとうございます：09886_arigatougozaimasu⟧: thank you for the invitation
- お{招|まね}きにあずかり、⟦{光栄|こうえい}→光栄：19436_kouei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{存|ぞん}じます→存じる：05912_zonjiru⟧: I am honored to have been invited
- ⟦{本日|ほんじつ}→本日：09643_honjitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お{招|まね}きにあずかり: today, being kindly invited (opening of a formal speech)
- ⟦{身|み}→身：01764_mi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{余|あま}る→余る：00001_amaru⟧お{招|まね}きにあずかる: to receive an invitation beyond what one deserves (very humble)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{招待|しょうたい}される→招待する：01833_shoutaisuru⟧: to be invited — plain, neutral equivalent.
- お⟦{招|まね}き→招く：02425_maneku⟧⟦いただく→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧: to be (kindly) invited — humble, but slightly less formal than あずかる; very common in business and formal writing.
- ご⟦{招待|しょうたい}→招待：01435_shoutai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧あずかる: synonymous variant using the Sino-Japanese noun ⟦{招待|しょうたい}→招待：01435_shoutai⟧; equally formal.
- お{呼|よ}ばれ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to be invited over (to someone's home) — softer, more colloquial.

REGISTER:
Humble, formal (⟦{謙譲語|けんじょうご}→謙譲語：15869_kenjougo⟧). Used by adults in formal public and professional settings; inappropriate in casual conversation.
